title: Pro-étale and étale ℓ-cohomological dimensions agree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a qcqs scheme $S$, a qcqs morphism $g\colon X\to Y$, and an integer $c\geq0$, using the scheme conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. All coefficient sheaves are abelian. Use the local $\ell$-power torsion convention of [sk-def-cd]: for $A[\ell^r]=\ker(\ell^r:A\to A)$, the canonical sheaf map $\varinjlim_{r\geq0}A[\ell^r]\to A$ is an isomorphism. Thus a section need only be killed by a power of $\ell$ locally on its site object, with no uniform exponent. The dimensions $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ and $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)$, the degree range $q\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and the suprema in $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\cup\{+\infty\}$ (empty supremum $0$) are as in [sk-def-cd]. Classical has the meaning of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]; the small sites and comparison morphisms $\nu$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The étale cohomology and direct-image notation is that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

1. For an abelian sheaf $F_0$ on $S_{\Et}$ and a classical sheaf $F\cong\nu_S^*F_0$ on $S_{\Proet}$, the sheaf $F$ is $\ell$-power torsion if and only if $F_0$ is.
2. $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)=\sup\{q:H^q(S_{\Et},F_0)\neq0\text{ for some }\ell\text{-power torsion sheaf }F_0\text{ on }S_{\Et}\}$.
3. $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)=\sup\{q:R^qg_{\Et,*}F_0\neq0\text{ for some }\ell\text{-power torsion sheaf }F_0\text{ on }X_{\Et}\}$.
4. If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(S)\leq c$ in the sense of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)\leq c$.

proof.text: (1) Work with discrete coefficients $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Put $L=\nu_S^*$ and $R=\nu_{S,*}$ in the module adjunction of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]; $L$ is exact and fully faithful. For each $r\geq0$ let $A_r=F_0[\ell^r]$. By the sectionwise kernel definition [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], exactness and additivity identify $L A_r$ with $(L F_0)[\ell^r]$: $L(\ell^r\operatorname{id}_{F_0})=\ell^r\operatorname{id}_{L F_0}$. These identifications respect the inclusions, because both maps compose with the kernel inclusions to the inclusion into $L F_0$. The required sheaf colimits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The adjunction proves that $L$ preserves them: a map $L(\varinjlim A_r)\to G$ is a map $\varinjlim A_r\to RG$, hence a compatible family of maps $A_r\to RG$, hence a compatible family $L A_r\to G$. Consequently applying $L$ to $a:\varinjlim A_r\to F_0$ gives precisely the torsion map $\varinjlim (L F_0)[\ell^r]\to L F_0$. A functor preserves isomorphisms, and full faithfulness reflects them: lift an inverse of $L a$ by fullness and use faithfulness to verify both inverse equations. The local torsion definition [sk-def-cd] therefore holds for $F_0$ exactly when it holds for $L F_0$, hence for the isomorphic $F$. This argument applies to every scheme and can also be used with $S$ replaced by $X$.

(2) By (1) and [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, the classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaves on $S_{\Proet}$ are, up to isomorphism, exactly the $
u_S^*F_0$ with $F_0$ an $\ell$-power torsion étale sheaf. The global-sections clause of [sk-prop-sf-comparison], applied to the bounded-below complex $F_0[0]$, gives $R\Gamma(S_{\Proet},
u_S^*F_0)\simeq R\Gamma(S_{\Et},F_0)$. Both sides are right derived functors of a left exact additive functor applied to a complex in degree zero, so by the uniqueness of $(RF,\eta)$ in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and its computation by any K-injective resolution, this is the $R\Gamma$ whose cohomology defines $H^q(S_{\Proet},-)$ in [sk-def-cd] and $H^q(S_{\Et},-)$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Taking degree $q$ cohomology gives $H^q(S_{\Proet},
u_S^*F_0)\cong H^q(S_{\Et},F_0)$. Thus the sets of nonvanishing degrees coincide with the set defining $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ in [sk-def-cd], so their suprema agree, also when the set is empty.

(3) Regard an $\ell$-power torsion étale sheaf $F_0$ on $X$ as $F_0[0]\in D^+(X_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$. The current arbitrary-discrete-commutative-ring comparison [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] applies to the given qcqs $g$, and gives $
u_Y^* Rg_{\Et,*}F_0\cong Rg_{\Proet,*}
u_X^*F_0$. Here $Rg_{\Proet,*}$ is the right derived functor of the direct image used in [sk-def-cd], unique up to unique isomorphism and computed by K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Exactness of $
u_Y^*$ from [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] identifies the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology, hence $
u_Y^* R^qg_{\Et,*}F_0\cong R^qg_{\Proet,*}
u_X^*F_0$. The same functor preserves zero objects by additivity and reflects them by faithfulness: if $
u_Y^*G=0$, then $
u_Y^*(\operatorname{id}_G)=0=
u_Y^*(0)$, so $\operatorname{id}_G=0$ and $G=0$. Applying (1) on $X$ and the classical-sheaf equivalence identifies all permitted inputs in the relative definition [sk-def-cd]. The two sets of nonvanishing degrees therefore coincide and have equal suprema. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed qcqs as a scheme; (1) and both comparison statements hold for arbitrary schemes. Only $g$ is required qcqs here.

(4) Let $F_0$ be an $\ell$-power torsion étale sheaf in the sense of [sk-def-cd]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (with $\mathcal O=\mathbf Z$), $\varinjlim_rF_0[\ell^r]$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise union $V\mapsto\bigcup_rF_0[\ell^r](V)\subseteq F_0(V)$, a separated subpresheaf of $F_0$; its sections are exactly the sections of $F_0$ that lie locally in this union. The canonical map to $F_0$ being an isomorphism, every $s\in F_0(U)$ has an étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and exponents $r_i$ with $\ell^{r_i}(s|_{U_i})=0$. Each $\ell^{r_i}$ is a positive integer since $\ell$ is prime. Hence such a sheaf satisfies the local torsion condition of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. Its cohomology consequently vanishes for $q>c$ if $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(S)\leq c$. By (2) every nonvanishing degree in the supremum defining $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ is at most $c$, so the supremum is at most $c$; the empty case also satisfies this because its supremum is $0$ and $c\geq0$.

Retained the four comparison clauses and all original hypotheses. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-batch (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement correction holds: binding ℓ and c≥0 and using sk-def-cd's local colimit torsion convention is faithful to the source. The literal global-annihilator reading is wrong (⊕Z/ℓ^n on an infinite disjoint union of points), and no node cites the item. All four clauses and the qcqs hypotheses on S and g are kept. Coefficients are abelian sheaves (Λ=Z), which the cited comparison nodes allow: they are stated for any (discrete commutative) ring. Replacing prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image with sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison keeps the proof on the unit's route. Step 1: ν* is exact, a left adjoint and fully faithful (det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules), so it preserves the kernels F[ℓ^r] and their colimit and reflects the isomorphism; this works for any scheme. Steps 2 and 3 match Stacks 099W and 09A6(2); step 3 uses exactly the qcqs hypothesis on g, and faithfulness detects zero. Step 4 is elementary. Edge cases pass: r=0, empty scheme or zero sheaf with supremum 0, g=id, a field, and ℓ equal to the characteristic. There are no new nodes. sk-def-cd's own proof steps 1–3 already prove clauses 1–3, which is redundancy, not a cycle. I accept lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful as a generic tool use. FIX: steps 2 and 3 now cite def-sfb-right-derived-functor (and step 2 def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology) so that sk-def-cd's derived-functor notation matches the comparison theorems. Step 4 now cites the colimit lemma, the sheafified union of the F[ℓ^r], to get local ℓ^r-annihilation from the colimit definition. proof_deps is updated; the corrected item file is in fixes/.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
